purpose: Supplementary source-discovered challenges, reported separately from the frozen 32-question development set without a before/after improvement claim. C03/C04 cover coordinated failure/re-entry. C05/C06 originated in the physics plan; C05 now routes current issue #10 policy. C07-C10 distinguish historical measured physics from current boundaries. C11/C12 cover current granular support and scheduled permeability.

questions.query: Why can powder pass through the player and Mercury pass through sand, and which tuning will help?
facts: The issue #9 baseline used a hard-surface-or-Sand predicate; current version 1 supports nine explicit powders through stable local packing, with stricter side resistance.
Current powder/powder density swaps are forbidden; real void movement and density-eligible liquid exchange remain distinct.
Mercury's current independent 30-tick lane slows exchange, with delayed waking and no exclusion catch-up. Its viscosity still controls lateral motion.

questions.query: How will barrels stop sinking at half depth, and how can rested materials become reversible Rapier objects?
facts: Audited current main does not contain the historically accepted #11 bounded granular-bearing/ejection repair; #81 owns source-matched current-main integration and #83 owns the broader body/granular gameplay envelope afterwards.
The historical #11 ordinary rectangle/load evidence remains valid in its recorded scope; reopening/repair routing does not erase it or imply broad acceptance.
Issue #12 is an independent scalable-soliding programme at Stage 3B; Stage 4 is blocked and #12 is not the sole remaining reason issue #8 is open.

questions.query: If a tick reports failure after hitting capacity, is it safe to retry as though nothing changed?
facts: Failed ticks may advance attempted tick/epoch and mutate cells/events; there is no rollback.
World latches failure and rejects further ticks/gameplay writes/publication; completed tick identity does not advance.
Desktop publishes stopped status retaining its last valid payload; Web pauses/menu-reports and suppresses partial output; Rapier stays main-thread owned.
Explicit reset/clear or validated replacement is required; accepted events are never automatically replayed and invalid replacement retains the fault.

questions.query: Will frozen offscreen sand resume automatically when the camera moves back, including the serial reference backend?
facts: Phased exclusion pauses ordinary rules and retains activity/quiet state; selected neighbor reach and explicit external writes/events remain possible.
At healthy tick entry newly included core coverage wakes resident blocks once, including sleepers; unchanged/equivalent/coalesced regions do not wake repeatedly. No elapsed-time catch-up.
SerialInPlace intentionally ignores the region; failed worlds cannot re-enter until clear/reset or validated replacement under the latest requested region.

questions.query: Can I shrink the camera window after a failed explosion tick and then resume the same world?
facts: No: shrinking only latches requested coverage; a failed world rejects ticks, activity transitions and gameplay mutations.
Explicit clear/reset or validated replacement abandons partial state/events and establishes fresh activity under the latest request. No rollback, retry or replay.

questions.query: Does panning by one pixel keep waking every settled cell or scanning the whole sparse world?
facts: Activity compares normalized core coverage at tick entry; equivalent/unchanged or coalesced windows do not repeatedly wake blocks.
Only newly included resident blocks wake; transition checks reuse existing metadata passes with no additional sparse-world scan, cell scan or allocation.
Selected core candidate capacity remains explicit and checked before deduplication; re-entry can fail under insufficient budget.

questions.query: Does raising Mercury viscosity slow downward penetration through packed Sand in the measured fixtures?
facts: In the historical issue #9 baseline, viscosity 96/160/224/248 gives identical confined vertical hashes and 32-tick breakthrough.
That baseline's isolated exchange veto is diagnostic only; current version 1 instead uses an independent 30-tick opportunity lane.
The dated reports separate source/artifact identities and screening budgets; period 30 gives 960-tick breakthrough in the current canonical bed.

questions.query: Does a barrel that stops at the bottom of a deep bed prove stable half-depth granular support?
facts: Depth uses the pre-impact datum plus a separate local deformed surface.
Hard-floor contact censors late creep; floor rest is not granular bearing.
The contact-off candidate is diagnostic only and still exceeds the provisional impact envelope.

questions.query: Why can retained powder inside a barrel generate downward impulses, and is increasing the cap sufficient?
facts: The issue #9 historical baseline showed proxy-derived downward contacts from stored powder under a body mask and showed that cap tuning alone did not establish intended support.
A later #11 source-matched checkpoint repaired masked-source feedback and ordinary bearing in a bounded envelope, but that accepted code is absent from audited current main.
#81 owns current-main integration of the bounded repair; #83 owns broad body/granular gameplay acceptance, so neither historical closure nor cap tuning is current broad acceptance.

questions.query: Did the barrel destroy the Water missing from the measured bed, or move it through the hard floor?
facts: The issue #9 full-world accounting control preserved all recorded Water mass and showed the cropped deficit below the hard floor: the defect was displacement across the barrier, not Water destruction.
The historical #11 repair added bounded barrier/body-mask-aware ejection in its accepted source-matched envelope, but audited current main again exposes the legacy endpoint-only target search.
#81 owns reconstruction/integration of the accepted bounded repair; current broad body/granular acceptance remains a later #83 question.

questions.query: Which current powders support a player, how do side resistance and enclosed-spawn recovery work, and why do loose grains still fall?
facts: Sand, Stone, Dust, Seed, Salt, Sodium, Gunpowder, Coal and Rust have explicit capability independent of density and hard identity.
Downward support needs 8/9 stable samples below the contact; side/head resistance additionally needs 9/9 centred samples.
Recovery tests at most 128 axis candidates within 32 cells, preserves cells, and explicitly blocks if no escape exists; it does not prove global connectivity or barrel bearing.

questions.query: How does the current Mercury permeability rate survive sleep and region exclusion without alternate attempts multiplying moves?
facts: Either liquid/powder initiator shares the global 30-tick lane; written destinations cannot be reused, while Empty motion bypasses the exchange gate.
Each source block stores its earliest due tick, woken by the existing healthy tick metadata pass; excluded blocks retain deadlines without catch-up.
Intact braced Stone is protected, other listed liquids keep explicit full-rate/Oil policies, and failed-world recovery discards deadlines with the old world.

questions.query: How do I author, validate and restart an Experiment Tower tuning profile, and which owner installs it?
facts: Version 1 profiles resolve defaults, family, material and explicit directed or symmetric pairs before tick work.
Desktop exclusive worker or synchronous Web owner installs a validated replacement; rejected candidates preserve the running world.
Profiles and resolved hashes are separate from CYSD1; ordinary gameplay stays Baseline.

questions.query: Does one horizontal sample preserve transport strength and improve total tick time, and can powder mixing be disabled separately?
facts: Sampling uses one existing deterministic candidate and does not compensate carrying strength.
Powder mixing is independent from Water carrying and only follows real powder movement.
Measure probes, transferred mass, active blocks, visited cells and total tick cost; reduced sampling is opt-in and no general speedup is claimed.

questions.query: Why does burning Coal leave a purple layer, and is that ash or another material?
facts: Burned-out Coal converts to Dust (14), whose RGBA color is 218,198,238,255.
Dust is the current residue; there is no separate Ash material. No reaction or fire cadence was changed for the Water follow-up.

questions.query: How was Water sideways flow made faster, and do the older transport profile hashes guarantee the same leveling?
facts: Water now requests three quarters of a lateral mass difference, with the same one-unit tolerance, two candidates, viscosity, film and coherence rules.
Water traces intentionally differ from the half-difference baseline, and optional grain pickup changes with actual flux.
Schema and resolved profile hashes remain unchanged; exact behavior requires source and artifact identity too.

questions.query: How can one MicroScenario definition run in Play Inspect Benchmark and load from JSON without separate physics scripts?
facts: Schema 1 validates bounded declarative data before native candidate replacement.
Existing desktop and synchronous owners share the same host; native-only headless runner refuses live character/body definitions.
New fixtures are exploratory apparatus, not #26 acceptance or #20 admission.

questions.query: Does a MicroScenario capture with source hashes restore the exact simulation and all user inputs?
facts: Capture is a definition plus observations, explicitly not complete replay or a restorable runtime snapshot.
Unknown revision/artifact identities stay unavailable; old publication identity is not substituted.
Scheduled Water edit deltas do not fabricate reactions, user-input or outflow accounting.

questions.query: What happens when a MicroScenario reset is rejected or an owner misses a scheduled event boundary?
facts: Rejected candidate preserves the previous World and host cursor.
Missed boundaries latch a fault, with no catch-up or automatic retry; native quarantine remains.
Captures crossing the desktop owner boundary are recursively frozen and retained safely.

questions.query: What exactly does MS-001 ship, what unblocks INT-000, and which platform claims remain separate?
facts: Materials Laboratory readiness is the specific checkpoint that can unblock issue 29; Flood Control and Stress are not additional prerequisites for INT-000.
MS-001 also contains a Flood-Control world-state puzzle and bounded Water/granular/gas/mixed Stress profiles on the same schema/host.
Exploratory source/functional completion, merged readiness and actual Windows/browser/target-GPU acceptance are distinct.

questions.query: How do I compare generated material definitions without changing a live worker and inspect temperature and scheduler work?
facts: A/B stores complete validated definitions and every load uses a fresh acknowledged reset.
One-cell probes report existing stored fields; masked temperature and per-cell sleep are not fabricated.
Native tick, host observer and whole-frame costs are distinct; unavailable counters remain explicit.

questions.query: Does the PR 23 one-island prototype complete scalable soliding and fracture issue 12?
facts: PR23 is retained Phase0 evidence; current-main successor begins from de332ea and preserves independent #26/#27 baselines.
Acceleration and Rapier macro-dynamics with coherent-child fracture are co-equal goals; later stages require genuine exit evidence.

questions.query: Does sleeping settled Sand qualify for rigid Rapier cohesion and can a fractured slab lose all rotation?
facts: Summary, stationary acceleration and dynamic cohesion are separate eligibility axes; rest never glues loose granular material.
Coherent children inherit parent translation and rotational point velocity; loose cellular motion loss must be explicit and measured.

questions.query: Can incremental settled block summaries prove connected world-scale discovery or a speedup over ordinary sleep?
facts: Block summaries are not connected regions; seams, holes, mixed states and complete bounded components remain Stage3 requirements.
Measure source-matched Current ordinary sleep and retain observer overhead, epoch work, failed results and missing metrics.

questions.query: How does the MS-001 Flood-Control puzzle prove multiple solutions and what does Simulation Stress Test actually measure?
facts: The untreated Flood definition wets the protected region while containment, berm and diversion definitions preserve the identical world-state objective and keep it dry using ordinary geometry only.
Stress uses finite existing setup/fill/erase operations under unchanged event and observation caps for Water, granular, gas and mixed workloads.
Available native work counters are reported with observer neutrality; unavailable queue, heap and per-worker-utilization counters are not invented.

questions.query: Issues 10 and 11 were completed, so are player and barrel granular interactions accepted and finished now?
facts: No single closed/completed bit answers the question: bounded #10 and historical #11 evidence remain valid, while later owner gameplay evaluation did not accept the broad player/body granular objectives.
#10 routes broad current player/granular acceptance to #82; #11 routes accepted bounded repair integration to #81 and broader body/granular acceptance to #83.
Issue #8 remains open and issue #12 is an independent soliding programme rather than the sole remaining blocker.

questions.query: What remediation issue owns each development-claims audit finding, and can Stage 3B continue while remediation runs?
facts: F01 routes to #81; broad F02 routes to #82/#83; formal Water H integrity to #84; F06-F11 stay with existing #49; current-truth/platform/counter cleanup goes to #85; closure/ownership/validation controls go to #86; #87 is the independent exit audit.
Stage 3B remains independently active: #61 has landed through PR #89; #62 then #63 are the serialized central-World continuation, while #64 is the separable graph/index lane before the #65 join.
Remediation does not impose a blanket Stage-3B pause; overlapping children must inspect live ownership/write sets and stop on a real collision rather than duplicate work.
